# controller-tools: generated manifests are wrong, empty, or crash the run — diagnosis without a test suite

Nothing survives a full run of this checkout, so it is worth starting with what goes wrong before any file at all is produced. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. The most immediate one is that almost every command pointed at a tree of Go sources dies with a nil pointer dereference while it is picking up the very first source group it was given, so it never reaches the point of emitting anything. Separately, when a run is handed a set of patterns naming which sources to bring in, the set it comes back with is wrong, and the ordinary case of a single pattern comes back empty; every later step then sees an empty world, reports no results, and stays silent about problems in the sources, so a map declared with a non-string key type, which should draw the complaint that keys must be strings, now passes without a word.

Once a tree can be examined at all, nothing you wrote in the comments above your declarations reaches what comes out. The descriptions sitting in those comments disappear, so emitted definitions carry no description text for types or fields even though the comment sits right above them. The annotations written in those comments fare no better: a sweep of a source group gathers none of them, so everything driven by comments — custom names, scopes, access entries, admission entries — comes out empty.
